description:
Returns the unanswered SpecPilot onboarding questions of the next incomplete step, gated by the answers so far: questions that do not apply are omitted, and options are filtered, badged or flagged as in the SpecPilot web chat. Stateless: send every answer collected so far on each call.

Procedure: (1) Set `isNewBuild` from whether the repo already has real source code. (2) Infer what the repo answers instead of asking: `platforms` from the manifests and layout, `languageOverride`, `ideAgent` (you are the IDE), `handle` from git config or the origin remote, `projectName` from the manifest or folder name, `projectDescription` from the README only if it plainly says what the project is. (3) Call this tool, answer what the repo makes obvious and ask the developer the rest, a whole step per message. Send an empty value for a declined optional question or it is asked again; send `todoSentinel` verbatim when they do not know yet. For `projectDescription`, an exact returned chip label infers `projectCategory` and gates later questions; free prose infers nothing. Confirm pre-seeded values rather than accepting them silently. (4) Loop until `done` is true, then call specpilot_generate_specs and follow its `nextSteps` for where each file goes.

answers.description: Every SpecPilot onboarding answer collected so far. The server is stateless, so resend the whole object on every call; omit it entirely on the first call to get step 1.

apiStyle.description: API style - REST, GraphQL, gRPC or tRPC.

availability.description: Availability SLA target as a fraction of uptime.

cicd.description: CI/CD practices - automatically running tests and deploying on every change.

compliance.description: Compliance regimes that apply - GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2. Pick by the actual situation (EU users, health data, payments).

constraintDescription.description: More detail on whatever was named in technicalConstraints.

customUserType.description: A user type in free text, when none of the userTypes options fit.

dataSyncStrategy.description: How conflicting local and server state gets reconciled once the device is back online.

databases.description: Database kinds in use - SQL, NoSQL, cache/key-value, vector. As many as apply.

deploymentTargets.description: Where this ships - cloud hosting, a package registry, a browser store. The option list depends on the project type.

handle.description: The developer GitHub handle. Optional. Infer from git config or the origin remote.

ideAgent.description: The editor or AI IDE in use - claudecode, cursor, copilot, codex, windsurf. You are the IDE, so set this yourself.

integrations.description: Third-party integrations keyed by category, e.g. { payments: ["stripe"] }. Only categories relevant to the project type apply.

isNewBuild.description: True for a greenfield project, false when adding onto an existing codebase.

languageOverride.description: Primary language, when it should override what SpecPilot infers from the repo.

localDatabases.description: On-device stores backing offline support. Leave empty when offline is not needed.

nonGoals.description: What this project explicitly will NOT do.

offlineSupport.description: Whether this has to work offline. Set automatically when localDatabases is non-empty.

otherApis.description: External APIs or services not covered by integrations.

projectDescription.description: One line saying what the project is. Required by specpilot_generate_specs. Sending one of the chip labels returned by specpilot_next_questions verbatim is what infers projectCategory and gates every later question; free prose infers nothing.

projectName.description: Short name for the project. Required by specpilot_generate_specs. Infer from the package manifest or the folder name.

realtimeEnabled.description: Whether anything updates live without a refresh. Set automatically when realtimeTypes is non-empty.

realtimeTypes.description: Realtime transports - WebSockets, SSE, polling. Leave empty when nothing needs to update live.

teamSize.description: How many people are building this.

technicalConstraints.description: Hard constraints - budget, existing infrastructure, legacy systems, a fixed deadline.

testingStrategy.description: Testing approaches this project will use.

userTypes.description: Who is going to use this system, e.g. end users, admins, internal staff.
